procedure_column: Navarro et al. 2024 (ACS ESC 8) Iron meteorites Spot analysis ns-LA-SF-ICP-MS University of Campinas

Procedure Name.cell: Navarro et al. (2024) Iron Meteorite Spot v1
Procedure Name.value: Navarro et al. (2024) Iron Meteorite Spot v1

Laboratory.cell: Isotope Geology Laboratory, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil
Laboratory.value: Isotope Geology Laboratory, University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil

Procedure Reference(s).cell: Navarro et al. (2024) ACS Earth Space Chem. 8, 281; Longerich et al. (1996)
Procedure Reference(s).value: Navarro et al. (2024) ACS Earth Space Chem. 8, 281; Longerich et al. (1996)

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Whole sample (polished ~1 cm fragment) > Spot — "fragments about 1 cm were mounted in epoxy resin, polished, and cleaned with ultrapure water" (p.3); the reported quantity is the meteorite's bulk composition for chemical classification (Table 1, p.2)

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Fragments ~1 cm mounted in epoxy resin, polished, cleaned with ultrapure water
Sample Preparation Method.value: Fragments ~1 cm mounted in epoxy resin, polished, cleaned with ultrapure water

Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.cell: Phase targeting, as the stated alternative to rastering — "depending on the specific objectives, spot sampling at specific phases may also fulfill the analytical requirements", against the problem that irons have an "inherent natural inhomogeneity, a result of their lamellar exsolution patterns" (p.2)
Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.value: Phase targeting, as the stated alternative to rastering

Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.cell: N — the preparation is stated without an imaging step: "Before analyses, fragments about 1 cm were mounted in epoxy resin, polished, and cleaned with ultrapure water" (p.3). The meteorites' structural classes were known beforehand (Table 1, p.2) but no screening of this material is described

ICP-MS Type.cell: Sector field (SF-ICP-MS) (explicitly stated: "sector field inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer")
ICP-MS Type.value: Sector field (SF-ICP-MS) (explicitly stated: "sector field inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer")

Interface Cone Configuration.cell: Ni sampler cone; Ni skimmer cone
Interface Cone Configuration.value: Ni sampler cone; Ni skimmer cone

Detector Configuration.cell: Triple mode detector (pulse counting, analog, Faraday)
Detector Configuration.value: Triple mode detector (pulse counting, analog, Faraday)

Laser Wavelength and Type.cell: 193 nm ArF excimer; pulse duration 4 ns
Laser Wavelength and Type.value: 193 nm ArF excimer; pulse duration 4 ns

Ablation Duration per Spot.cell: 40 s on-sample ablation (after 20 s background measurement)
Ablation Duration per Spot.value: 40 s on-sample ablation (after 20 s background measurement)

Carrier Gas and Flow Rate.cell: He: 0.6 l min⁻¹ (MFC 1) + 0.7 l min⁻¹ (MFC 2) in HelEx II cell; combined with Ar makeup via T-piece near torch
Carrier Gas and Flow Rate.value: He: 0.6 l min⁻¹ (MFC 1) + 0.7 l min⁻¹ (MFC 2) in HelEx II cell; combined with Ar makeup via T-piece near torch

Make-up Gas and Flow Rate.cell: Ar make-up gas (combined via T-piece in sample transport line near torch; flow rate not stated separately)
Make-up Gas and Flow Rate.value: Ar make-up gas (combined via T-piece in sample transport line near torch; flow rate not stated separately)

Coolant (Plasma) Gas Flow Rate.cell: Plasma gas: 16 l min⁻¹; Auxiliary: 0.9 l min⁻¹; Nebulizer gas (from table): 1.1 l min⁻¹
Coolant (Plasma) Gas Flow Rate.value: Plasma gas: 16 l min⁻¹; Auxiliary: 0.9 l min⁻¹; Nebulizer gas (from table): 1.1 l min⁻¹

ICP Tuning.cell: ICP and laser settings optimized daily for optimum signal intensity and low oxide formation (factory specifications; mass calibration and detector cross-calibration checked and redone if required)
ICP Tuning.value: ICP and laser settings optimized daily for optimum signal intensity and low oxide formation (factory specifications; mass calibration and detector cross-calibration checked and redone if required)

Oxide Production Method and Threshold.cell: N (factory optimization criterion; exact threshold not stated)

Analysis Sequence.cell: NIST SRM 612(×3) → North Chile(×3) → unknowns(×10) → NIST SRM 612(×2) → North Chile(×2) → unknowns(×10) → … (bracketing every 15)
Analysis Sequence.value: NIST SRM 612(×3) → North Chile(×3) → unknowns(×10) → NIST SRM 612(×2) → North Chile(×2) → unknowns(×10) → … (bracketing every 15)

Target Species.cell: ⁵²Cr, ⁵⁷Fe, ⁵⁹Co, ⁶¹Ni, ⁶⁵Cu, ⁶⁹Ga, ⁷²Ge, ⁷⁵As, ⁹⁹Ru, ¹⁰³Rh, ¹⁰⁵Pd, ¹⁸²W, ¹⁸⁵Re, ¹⁸⁹Os, ¹⁹³Ir, ¹⁹⁵Pt, ¹⁹⁷Au (17 isotopes); low relative abundance isotopes chosen for Ni and Fe (analog mode)

value.member: low relative abundance isotopes chosen for Ni and Fe

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species

Reported Variables and Units.cell: Elemental mass fractions in metal, with units mixed by magnitude — As, Au, Co, Cu, Ga, Ge, Ir, Pd, Ru and others in µg g-1, Fe and Ni in g/100 g (Table 5, p.12) — reported with 2 sdm; the derived output is the meteorite's chemical classification (nominal, Table 1, p.2)

Dwell Time per Mass.cell: 0.02 s per isotope; 100 samples per peak; 10 runs; 60 passes; total measurement time 120 s per analysis

Background Count Time.cell: 20 s background measurement (laser shutter closed) before each 40 s ablation
Background Count Time.value: 20 s background measurement (laser shutter closed) before each 40 s ablation

Inter-Pass Data Dependency.cell: Single acquisition run (20 spot analyses per sample under repeatability conditions)

Number of Replicates.cell: 20 spot analyses per meteorite under repeatability conditions; additional measurements on different days
Number of Replicates.value: 20 spot analyses per meteorite under repeatability conditions; additional measurements on different days

Internal Standard Approach.cell: Fe+Ni+Co sum normalization to 100% using iolite 3D Trace Elements DRS (eliminates need for independent EPMA IS)

Internal Standard Element.cell: No single IS; Fe+Ni+Co mass fractions normalized to 100% via iolite 3D DRS (yield correction factors applied for NIST SRM 612 relative to North Chile)

Elemental Fractionation Correction.cell: External calibration using North Chile iron meteorite + NIST SRM 612 glass (yield correction applied in iolite 3D DRS for NIST relative to North Chile); ordinary least-squares fitting per 15 min calibration block; Fe+Ni+Co normalization eliminates need for independent EPMA IS

Uncertainty Propagation Method.cell: N (iolite 4 computes uncertainty internally via Longerich et al. 1996)

Matrix Offset Correction (LIEF).cell: N (yield correction in iolite DRS addresses relative sensitivity differences between NIST SRM 612 and North Chile)

Signal Integration Interval Method.cell: Time-resolved LA-ICP-MS signals inspected per analysis; background interval (20 s) and ablation interval (40 s) selected; no automated spike exclusion described
Signal Integration Interval Method.value: Time-resolved LA-ICP-MS signals inspected per analysis; background interval (20 s) and ablation interval (40 s) selected; no automated spike exclusion described

Spike / Outlier Filtering Approach.cell: N (no explicit spike filtering described beyond background subtraction)

Blank / Background Correction Method.cell: Background signal measured for 20 s (laser shutter closed) before each 40 s ablation; background mean subtracted per isotope in iolite
Blank / Background Correction Method.value: Background signal measured for 20 s (laser shutter closed) before each 40 s ablation; background mean subtracted per isotope in iolite

Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Corre.cell: Applied: triple mode detector (pulse counting, analog, Faraday); low relative abundance isotopes chosen for Ni and Fe to allow analog mode measurement of major matrix elements

value.value: triple mode detector (pulse counting, analog, Faraday)

Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.cell: Yes — isotope selection to minimize interferences (e.g., ⁹⁹Ru instead of ¹⁰¹Ru to avoid ⁴⁰Ar⁶¹Ni⁺; low abundance isotopes for Fe and Ni)

Interfering Species.cell: ⁴⁰Ar⁶¹Ni⁺ on ¹⁰¹Ru (primary concern) → ⁹⁹Ru used instead; Fe and Ni matrix species on other isotopes minimized by isotope selection

Interference Correction Method.cell: Isotope selection minimizes interferences; low-abundance isotopes of Fe and Ni chosen for analog mode to prevent detector saturation

Memory Effect Mitigation.cell: N (washout between analyses not explicitly described; sequential spot analyses)

Normalization / Standards-Based Correcti.cell: Fe+Ni+Co=100% sum normalization applied in iolite 3D Trace Elements DRS as final step; yield correction factors applied for NIST SRM 612 relative to North Chile

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially — contributing counts are stated ('n: number of replicates'; 'the mean value of 20 spot measurements in the Arraias meteorite'); no acceptance or rejection rule is stated

Combination Method.cell: all: average of n replicate spot measurements per meteorite — 'average (x̅); s: standard deviation of n measured values'; 'the mean value of 20 spot measurements in the Arraias meteorite'

value.value: average of n replicate spot measurements per meteorite

Primary Calibration Standard Name.cell: NIST SRM 612 glass (Jochum et al. 2011) + North Chile Filomena iron meteorite (Wasson et al. 1989) — used together with yield correction in iolite 3D DRS

Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.cell: NIST SRM 612 and North Chile measured bracketing every 15 unknowns: 3×STD → 3×STD → 10×unknowns → repeat
Calibration Standard Measurement Frequen.value: NIST SRM 612 and North Chile measured bracketing every 15 unknowns: 3×STD → 3×STD → 10×unknowns → repeat

Secondary Reference Materials.cell: North Chile Filomena measured as unknown on different days over 4 months to assess intermediate precision (Table 3 and Fig. 2)

value.member: North Chile Filomena measured as unknown on different days over 4 months to assess intermediate precision

Detection Limit.cell: LODs in µg g⁻¹ (median from Table 3): As 2, Au 0.1, Co 2, Cr 19, Cu 0.8, Fe 5300, Ga 0.1, Ge 0.2, Ir 0.04, Ni 60, Os 0.09, Pd 0.06, Pt 0.4, Re 0.02, Rh 0.05, Ru 0.3, W 0.09; calculated per Longerich et al. (1996) in iolite 4

members: LODs in µg g⁻¹ (median from Table 3)

Detection Limit Method.cell: Longerich et al. (1996) — implemented in iolite 4; sample-individual LOD calculated per analysis

Counting Statistics Error.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Within-Session Analytical Precision and.cell: RSD <15% for most elements in Arraias meteorite under repeatability conditions (n=20 spot analyses); Cr: 20%, Ir: 16%, Os: 20% RSD; assessed by repeated analysis of same meteorite in one session

Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical P.cell: Intermediate precision: RSD ≤20% for most elements assessed over multiple days on North Chile iron meteorite measured as unknown (n multiple days over 4 months)

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: Results for 9 known iron meteorites: >75% of published values within LA-ICP-MS result ± 2s (two standard deviations); relative differences mostly within ±20% (Fig. 2); specific discrepancies: Ir in Arraias +40%, Ir in Nossa Senhora +64%, Co and Ga in Campo del Cielo (heterogeneity issues); trend lines slope 0.87–1.17 with R² = 0.97–1.0

Additional Notes.cell: Key innovations: (1) use of two measurement standards (NIST SRM 612 + North Chile) with yield correction in iolite 3D DRS; (2) Fe+Ni+Co=100% normalization eliminates need for EPMA IS; Cr results not quantitative due to argide interferences
Additional Notes.value: Key innovations: (1) use of two measurement standards (NIST SRM 612 + North Chile) with yield correction in iolite 3D DRS; (2) Fe+Ni+Co=100% normalization eliminates need for EPMA IS; Cr results not quantitative due to argide interferences
